scoring_justification: Full recompute from raw artifacts infeasible (only final CSV curves provided); scoring uses structural/shape properties: specific heat upturn detection, resonant peak windows, log-log slope for thermal conductivity.

hidden_assets.purpose: Hidden structural thresholds for specific heat upturn ratio, impurity peak windows and minimum height, thermal conductivity slope target and tolerance.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Derived from paper's claims: low-T upturn in C_V/T (Fig. 6), resonant peaks near Mott gap edges (Fig. 7b), and T^{-2} scaling of κ_f (Fig. 5c and text).
hidden_assets.generation_method: Thresholds chosen to be broad enough to accept any honest reproduction while rejecting curves lacking the required physical features; no exact digitized data from the figure is embedded.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Thresholds are generic physically motivated bounds, not arbitrary numbers, and any correct implementation of the paper's equations will satisfy them.

outputs.description: Electronic specific heat divided by temperature (C_V/T) as a function of T^2, expected to show a low-temperature upturn consistent with experimental data.
Impurity electron spectral function A_d(ω) displaying resonant peaks near the Mott gap edges.
Spinon thermal conductivity κ_f as a function of temperature, approximately following a T^{-2} scaling.

output_contract.notes: All scored artifacts are produced by computing relevant quantities from the self-consistently determined Green's functions and effective interactions. The checker will compare the specific heat curve to a hidden experimental reference (RMSE-based), verify the structural properties of the impurity spectral peaks (position and height), and confirm the approximate -2 slope of the log–log thermal conductivity.

steps.description: Verify the C_V/T vs T^2 curve exhibits a low-temperature upturn: C_V/T at the lowest T^2 values is significantly higher than the value predicted by a linear fit through the higher T^2 points.
Detect resonant peaks in A_d(ω) within ±0.1 eV of the Mott gap edges (±0.5 eV). Verify that at least one peak appears in each window and that peak heights exceed a minimum threshold.
Fit log10-log10 linear regression to κ_f vs T and verify the slope is within -2 ± 0.3.
